Ratatat shares the inspiration behind each track of Magnifique.

This is a cool collection of stories behind each song.

I just wish they shared a little about the outro. Which I love.

This one started with the idea of playing two separate guitar melodies simultaneously with neither one playing a supporting role to the other. Instead, we wanted the guitars playing dual leads, one in each ear. We’re constantly layering guitars in our music, but in this song the guitars aren’t harmonizing, they’re each playing a completely different character. Of course as the song develops it all comes together as more and more layers join in, but it all stems from the initial idea of these two individual characters pushing forward alongside one another.

I really LOVE this song, Rome. The guitar in the right speaker reminds me of "Built to Spill" and the other guitar reminds me of some classical stuff. It's simply a work that shows Ratatat's versatility. About half way through the song they transform into the Pixies or Modest Mouse for a few bars followed by more transformations as the song progresses. It's just this gentle transition from one style to another, one technique to another yet it stays, somehow, mysteriously, on the same motif. It just speaks to my soul and moves me every time I listen.

Everyone who has a muscle car and wants to modify it starts with a cold air induction kit, it's really easy to install, not-so-expensive, and supposedly provides extra power. But if that was truly the case, why wouldn't car manufacturers do this process themselves? I'm pretty sure Ford/Chevy/Dodge wouldn't want to miss out on the benefits of even 10 extra horses, as the competition is pretty tough right now. Did all of the engineers working for hundreds of hours on these cars just happened to forget about adding a cold air induction kit?
My thoughts on cold air induction kits

It is true that an engine burns more efficiently at cooler temperatures, but I really doubt you are going to see anywhere near a ten percent increase in horsepower. All that a cold air induction kit does is send a tube to a spot in the engine bay where the air is cool, like the front off to the side, and then they put an expensive air filter on there that needs to be oiled and cleaned instead of being changed. Most new cars already get the intake air from a similar location, and a stock air filter, if regularly changed, will allow plenty of air past without needing the care and maintenance of a lifetime filter. So to answer your question, yes, manufacturers already do this.
Same thing if you got a hundred horses.
Yeah, but how many cars only have a hundred hp these days?
A mixture between costs and keeping things quiet I imagine.

Cold air intakes do nothing but make you feel a little better when someone asks you, so what you got under the hood? Oh i have a BBK cold air intake and a Borla exhaust! If you don't believe me take your car to a dyno and swap out the intake box between runs.

Some cold air intakes actually pick up air from the bottom of the engine compartment, that's a big no-no for car manufacturers because people expect their cars to be able to drive through somewhat deep puddles, or may just go through them unknowingly. Those CAIs can, and do, provide a convenient means for significant amounts of water to make its way into the engine. Noise is another big issue. Many modern cars have a somewhat restrictive intake path in order to muffle intake noise.
Engineers are restricted by cost, emissions, and perception of noise/driving comfort.
I have never seen any noticeable increase in power from a cold air kit. All they do is make the engine noisier and your wallet lighter. Save your money.
My 87 MR2 has it's air intake in the boot. Does that count as standard cold air induction? I get a couple of extra kilowatts with the boot open.

Realistically, cold air intakes don't do anything. They are for people who want to feel like they know how to 'work on cars' and have cool upgrades on their mediocre civics. Cool air intake + exhaust + body kit + new shift knob ...
To be fair, a full exhaust upgrade can improve your numbers. Cat-back/new can: not so much

Cold Air Intake works - usually it is a smoother pipe getting air away from the heat soaked engine. It should be combined with better exhaust. The engine is essentially an air compressor, air pump. The easier is to get air in and out the better it works. :)

A lot of the stuff on a car's engine is put there to meet emissions regulations, take the noise level down, and keep from sucking up bugs and water. This video is pretty interesting. Its not all about power for the manufacturers. Some people don't want to hear the noises their car/truck makes. Manufacturers are building cars that are going to make a lot of people happy enough. They're more than willing to let the after market industry finish the job.
